title: 30-day return to hospital after same-day discharge hip arthroplasty (STAR)

answers.study/department: Department of Anesthesia and Pain Management, Toronto Western Hospital. The study looks at the STAR (Short Term Accelerated Recovery) same-day discharge program, which Anesthesia runs with Orthopaedic Surgery and Physiotherapy.
answers.study/summary: STAR is our same-day discharge pathway for primary total hip arthroplasty and has been running since Oct 15, 2018. We have never followed up on what happens to these patients after they go home. This chart review counts returns to hospital for surgical problems within 30 days (and 7 days) of surgery, and compares patients sent home the same day with STAR patients who stayed at least one night and with patients taken off the pathway before surgery. Records only, no patient contact. The results tell us whether the program is safe and will help size a future prospective study.
answers.classification/question: Is the rate of return to hospital for surgery-related problems in the first 30 days different for STAR patients discharged home on the day of surgery, compared with STAR-eligible patients who stayed at least one night and with patients removed from STAR before surgery? Secondary: the same comparison at 7 days, and the age and gender of each group.
answers.classification/cohort/population: Everyone flagged by their surgeon as potentially STAR eligible when booked for primary THA at Toronto Western, from the start of the program. They are flagged before the physio and anesthesia STAR assessments, so the cohort includes patients who were later found ineligible. Patients who never came to surgery are excluded. Three groups: eligible and discharged same day, eligible but not discharged same day, removed from STAR before surgery.
answers.classification/cohort/dateRationale: Starts the day STAR began (Oct 15, 2018). Surgeries up to Oct 1, 2019, by when we expect about 120 patients to have been screened, plus 30 days of follow-up after the last surgery.
answers.classification/sources/sourceDetails: 1. STAR enrolment list kept by the PI (program list of everyone flagged at booking). 2. UHN electronic patient record: the surgical admission and any return to a UHN emergency department or ward within 30 days. 2018-19 encounters are in the legacy EPR, viewable through Epic. 3. ConnectingOntario ClinicalViewer, looked up per patient, to catch visits to other hospitals, since STAR patients live within an hour's drive and may go to their local ED. No CAPCR numbers apply.
answers.identifiability/fields: Key list (PI only): name, date of birth, MRN, date of surgery, age and gender, against a Patient Study Number. Name, DOB and MRN are needed to pull each chart at UHN and in ConnectingOntario. Coded REDCap forms: study number, cohort, removal from STAR and reason, same-day discharge and reason if not, PACU arrival and discharge times, length of stay, days in hospital, return encounter Y/N, days post-op at return, nature of the surgical problem, anesthesia checklist complete. No names, DOB or MRN go into REDCap.
answers.identifiability/reidentification: Identifiers stay on one key list held by the PI, separate from all the data sheets. REDCap holds study numbers only. Paper copies of the key given to chart reviewers are handed over in person and shredded once collection is done. The statistician never sees identifiers. Surgery dates are not in the analysis file, only days post-op.
answers.identifiability/linkageRisk: Each patient is looked up in ConnectingOntario by name and DOB to see if they had a hospital visit elsewhere in the 30 days. We only record whether there was a visit, how many days post-op, and what the surgical problem was. Nothing else from the provincial record is copied, so the coded file is no more identifying than the UHN data on its own.
answers.consent/waiver/whyIdentifiable: We have to find each patient's charts, at UHN and in ConnectingOntario, and the only way to do that is by name, DOB and MRN. Returns to another hospital can't be found any other way. Identifiers are used only for the look-up and never go into the analysis data.
answers.access/custodian: UHN for the UHN record; Ontario Health for ConnectingOntario
answers.handling/storage/access: Key list: PI only, in his folder on the UHN network drive. Paper copies of parts of it go to the chart reviewers by hand and are shredded when their charts are done. REDCap (UHN instance): the PI, department members and trained medical students on the delegation log, each with their own login. The statistician gets read-only export rights on the coded data and runs R on a UHN virtual desktop, so no copy leaves UHN. Accounts are removed when people leave the study.
answers.handling/storage/retentionPeriod: Key destroyed once the analysis is final; coded data kept 7 years after publication
answers.handling/results/incidental: The returns we're looking at happened in 2018-19 and were handled clinically at the time. If a chart shows a problem that looks like it was never followed up, the PI will let the patient's surgeon know. Any safety pattern in the program goes to the STAR committee.
answers.digital/usage: UHN REDCap for coded data entry: one form per cohort, built by the team from the spreadsheet headings in the SAP. No surveys, no participant access.
answers.resources/other: A few days of the statistician's time for the chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests.

weaknesses: Small cells: handling/results/reporting is 'aggregate' with no suppression rule, but only about 24 patients go home the same day and the SAP already expects 2x2 cells small enough to need Fisher's exact test, so published counts of returns will be 1 to 5 people.

Linking key storage: the form says the key list is on the PI's UHN network drive (storage/location 'server', no policy deviation), while the protocol (p. 4) and the SAP (p. 2) still say it lives on a password protected personal computer hard drive. The protocol needs amending, or the form is wrong.

screening.summary: A small, records-only cohort study of about 120 STAR hip arthroplasty patients, with a sensible coding scheme and a clear analysis plan. Two things need tidying: the protocol's description of where the linking key is kept doesn't match the form, and results have no small-cell rule although several cells will be tiny. Custodian approval for the provincial record look-ups is still pending.

assessments.summary: Records only, no contact, and the data comes from care records and the STAR program list. Research is the right classification: the study tests a hypothesis and is meant to size a future prospective study.
The protocol calls the work quality assurance throughout, while the form files it as research.

comments.text: The protocol describes the study as quality assurance in the objective, the design and the conclusion, but the form classifies it as research. The form is right, given the hypothesis testing and the plan to inform a future study, but the protocol's wording could lead someone to treat it as exempt QA later.
comments.suggestion: Amend the protocol to describe the work as a retrospective cohort research study.
comments.quote: This project is a retrospective cohort quality assurance study.

assessments.summary: Coded data with the key held by the PI, kept apart from all data sheets. Proportionate for a 120-patient chart review.

comments.text: The SAP compares age and gender across the three cohorts, but in its spreadsheet layout those two columns appear only on the De-identifier sheet that holds the names, DOB and MRN. As written, the statistician would need the key sheet to run the demographic comparison.
comments.suggestion: Copy age and gender into the coded All Patient List (Spreadsheet 2) and keep them off the key list, or confirm they will be in the REDCap forms.
comments.quote: Demographic data (age and gender) will be statistically compared between the three cohorts as follows.

assessments.summary: Each condition is argued. Identifiers are needed only to find charts, there's no foreseeable effect on welfare, and a 30-day safety rate needs the whole cohort, since patients who had complications may well answer a consent request differently.
UHN data is covered by PHIPA s. 44 once approved. The provincial record look-ups need Ontario Health's approval, which is still pending.

comments.text: Looking up every patient in ConnectingOntario is research use of a system whose access terms are written for clinical care. Approval from Ontario Health is marked pending, and the look-ups are central to the primary outcome.
comments.suggestion: Make approval conditional on Ontario Health's written approval, and file it with the REB before any look-ups begin.
comments.quote: It is for this reason that the BC Care Connect network will be accessed for each patient

assessments.summary: The only linkage is a per-patient look-up of outside hospital visits, and only the visit, its timing and the surgical problem are recorded. The coded file gains nothing identifying from it.
Good separation of key and data, and paper copies are shredded after collection. Where the key lives is inconsistent between the form and the protocol.

comments.text: The form says the key list is kept on the UHN network drive, with no deviation from the records policy. The protocol and the SAP both say it is kept on a password protected personal computer hard drive, which would not meet UHN policy for identifiable data.
comments.suggestion: Confirm the key is on the UHN network drive or an encrypted UHN device, and amend the protocol and SAP to match.
comments.quote: This linked data will be stored only on a password protected personal computer hard drive retained by the PI

assessments.summary: Results are aggregate, but with no rule for small counts in a cohort this small.

comments.text: Only about 24 patients went home the same day, and the SAP already expects cells small enough to need Fisher's exact test. Return counts of one to five patients, broken down by days post-op and the nature of the problem, could point to individuals, especially for staff who know the program.
comments.suggestion: Set a suppression threshold (commonly fewer than 5) for counts in tables and the text, and describe complications in categories rather than case by case.
comments.quote: unless expected values are less than 10 (with degrees of freedom of 1) in which case Fisher’s Exact Test will be used

assessments.summary: Inclusion is everyone flagged at booking, the only exclusion is not having surgery, and the SAP moves to Fisher's exact test for small counts. The groups differ in fitness by design, which the protocol accepts by presenting this as a preliminary safety assessment.
Records run from October 2018 to October 2019, well in the past, so no one is still in follow-up.
The only tool is UHN's own REDCap instance, the statistician works on a UHN virtual desktop, and nothing leaves UHN. Nothing to raise.
